reasoning: Both sets are well built and share a pipeline/contract/packet method. A matches the user's ground truth more closely. It specifies the Yahoo cross-check through yahooquery (XCHK-01–05) and a reference-list check of the user's 10 delisted names (CHECK-09). It has a thorough S2: Marchenko–Pastur band, sample, constant-correlation shrinkage, denoised and factor estimators, then min-variance, ERC and HRP on every estimator, with synthetic known-answer gates and a family-corrected test routed to null-hypothesis-testing. It also has an explicit frontend-design approval task that comes before every view task, and it handles RF-01's whole-sample PCA flaw with a per-window refit (AD-16). A's main gaps: S4 drops the PPO agents, which become 'a later stage', and it rules out the rented GPU the user has. Its plan also has a stale 'SSE' title and some false serialization (T13–T15 waiting on T12). B covers S4 fully: LSTM and TFT-lite forecasters, PPO agents with budgets, GPU bundles with verified teardown, a lockbox and a verdict. Its hypothesis ledger is a strong null-testing handoff. But B drops the user's Yahoo cross-check entirely and never checks the 10 named delisted stocks, which are core S1 requirements. It adds sources nobody asked for (FRED, EDGAR SIC) and an invented 5% weight cap. Its first S2 milestone runs on real data instead of starting as a synthetic walking skeleton. Every packet cites CONSTRAINTS.md, but B has no CONSTRAINTS.md file, and several packets mark files as '(new)' that earlier tasks already created. Both sets wrongly route Sharadar through Nasdaq Data Link instead of its own API at api.sharadar.com. On balance A's S1–S3 accuracy and its build discipline outweigh B's more complete S4.
